name: 46,XX Difference of Sex Development

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Statement on Management of Differences of Sex Development

criteria.description: Presence of 46,XX karyotype confirmed by cytogenetic analysis
Clinical evidence of atypical external genitalia such as clitoromegaly or labioscrotal fusion
Abnormal androgen levels inconsistent with typical female hormonal profile
Imaging evidence of internal reproductive structures inconsistent with typical female anatomy
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes involved in sex differentiation (e.g., SRY translocation, SOX9 duplication)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of 46,XX karyotype plus clinical evidence of atypical genitalia and abnormal androgen levels
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including genetics, endocrinology, and radiology

pathognomonic.symptomName: Presence of 46,XX karyotype with virilized external genitalia

searchTerms: problems with urinary and genital openings

common.symptomName: Hirsutism in infancy or early childhood
searchTerms: hair growth in infants or toddlers

common.symptomName: Palpable gonadal tissue in labioscrotal folds

searchTerms: urethra opening on underside of penis

occasional.symptomName: Psychosocial distress related to gender ambiguity
searchTerms: emotional problems due to ambiguous genitalia
hernia with gonadal tissue in groin
high blood pressure from adrenal enlargement
hypertension due to adrenal gland problem
blood pressure raised by adrenal hyperplasia

rare.symptomName: Adrenal crisis in cases with congenital adrenal hyperplasia
searchTerms: acute adrenal failure in congenital adrenal hyperplasia

laboratory: Abnormal 17-hydroxyprogesterone levels in congenital adrenal hyperplasia
Hormonal assays showing disrupted hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis
imaging: Pelvic ultrasound showing presence or absence of uterus and ovaries
MRI of pelvis for detailed gonadal anatomy
Genitography to assess urogenital sinus anatomy
genetic: SRY gene translocation or duplication detected by FISH or PCR
Mutations in CYP21A2, SOX9, or other sex differentiation genes
other: Histopathological examination of gonadal tissue if biopsy performed
Psychological assessment for gender identity and support

distinguishingFeatures: Female external genitalia with absent uterus
Elevated testosterone with androgen receptor mutations

redFlags: Severe virilization of external genitalia at birth
Salt-wasting crisis or adrenal insufficiency symptoms
Rapid onset of puberty or virilization in childhood
references: Hughes IA, et al. Consensus statement on management of differences of sex development. Nat Rev Endocrinol. 2006.
Lee PA, et al. Global DSD Update: Consensus on DSD Management. Horm Res Paediatr. 2016.
